newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices end volatile day down.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices end volatile day down.

text.p: Danish bond prices closed lower on Monday, with U.S. CPI data failing to give them an expected lift and the strike-fearing French market casting a pall over the Copenhagen bourse.
"Its been a rather strange day, with the (Danish) benchmark swinging about a half point," said a dealer who expected Thursday's trade to be similar.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 slipped 0.04 point from Tuesday's close to 107.66 in turnover of 3.8 billion crowns.
The dealer saw it trading between 107.75 and 108.25.
The benchmark's December future fell 0.08 point to 107.34, with 217 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.10 point to 85.18.

The crown traded down to 3.8311 per mark from its earlier 3.8302 and the 10-year yield gap with Germany ended the day at 83 basis points, compared to Tuesday's 82 bp. --Eva Elgaard Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969651
